questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: For the power-of-a-power property to hold, (7^(1/4))⁴ must equal 7^((1/4)·4) = 7. What number must 7^(1/4) be? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
For the power-of-a-power property to hold, (7^(1/4))⁴ must equal 7^((1/4)·4) = 7.
What number must 7^(1/4) be? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: ⁴√7, the fourth root of 7 (the positive number whose fourth power is 7).
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent form, such as the fourth root of 7. The explanation must use the fact that (7^(1/4))⁴ = 7.

questions.skill: Use the inverse relationship between exponents and logarithms
questions.standard_level: Precalculus. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Precalculus, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: f(x) = 10^x and g(x) = log x (log means base 10). Find f(g(100)) and g(f(2)), and say what they show.
questions.prompt_markup:
f(x) = 10^x and g(x) = log x (log means base 10).
Find f(g(100)) and g(f(2)), and say what they show.
questions.correct_answer: f(g(100)) = 100 and g(f(2)) = 2: f and g undo each other, so they are inverse functions.
questions.grading_note: Form required: both values and the conclusion. g(100) = 2 and f(2) = 100.

questions.prompt: A sound level is L = 10 log(I ÷ I₀) decibels, where log means base 10. Solve for the intensity I in terms of L.
questions.prompt_markup:
A sound level is L = 10 log(I ÷ I₀) decibels, where log means base 10.
Solve for the intensity I in terms of L.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent form. Divide by 10, then use 10 to the power of each side: I ÷ I₀ = 10^(L/10).

questions.prompt: Which function is the inverse of f(x) = 5^x?
questions.prompt_markup: Which function is the inverse of f(x) = 5^x?
questions.grading_note: log₅ x undoes 5^x: log₅(5^x) = x and 5^(log₅x) = x for x > 0.
